summary: Serbia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says holders of ordinary passports of, for example, Germany, the US and the UK need no visa for visits of up to 90 days in a 6-month period from the first entry, and that ordinary-passport holders of Russia, China and Belarus need none for visits of up to 30 days, and of the UAE and Bahrain for up to 90 days within 6 months. Under a 2014 Government decision, holders of a valid Schengen, UK, EU member state or US visa, or of a Schengen, EU or US residence permit, can also enter without a Serbian visa. Visa applications are submitted to a Serbian embassy or consulate general abroad or online.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says you must declare personal items of value you are carrying, for example jewellery, cameras and computing equipment, and that these are exempt from customs duties. Canada says these items should be intended for your own personal use and you must take them with you when leaving the country.

The UK Foreign Office says that if you take any Serbian dinars into the country you must show the receipt from the bank where you bought them, and that you should exchange any unwanted dinars before you leave.

safety.text: Canada's travel advice says to take normal security precautions in Serbia and a high degree of caution within 10km of the border with Kosovo, due to the potential for political tensions, possible civil unrest and the presence of landmines. It says violent demonstrations have taken place across the country, and that petty crime such as pickpocketing occurs, with thieves targeting tourists in crowded public areas such as buses, trains, stations and airports.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says that to travel from Kosovo to Serbia you must have a Serbian entry stamp from Belgrade, Niš or Kraljevo airports or from one of Serbia's land border crossings with its other neighbours, and that without one you are likely to be refused entry. Canada says not to attempt to enter Serbia directly from Kosovo unless you initially travelled into Kosovo from Serbia and obtained a valid Serbian entry stamp, and otherwise to transit via a third country such as Albania, North Macedonia or Montenegro.

The UK Foreign Office says it is aware of isolated incidents where Serbian authorities have cancelled Kosovo stamps in passports of foreign nationals or denied foreign nationals entry to Serbia if they have Republic of Kosovo stamps in their passports.

The UK Foreign Office says you must register with the local police where you are staying within 24 hours of arrival. Canada says registration will normally be arranged by your hotel or host, and that failure to register can result in fines and difficulties when departing.

The UK Foreign Office says not to use street dealers and to change money only through banks or official exchange offices, and to exchange any unwanted dinars before you leave Serbia, as British banks do not normally exchange dinars.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Serbia?
faq.answer: Serbia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says holders of ordinary passports of, for example, Germany, the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand need no visa for visits of up to 90 days in a 6-month period from the first entry; ordinary-passport holders of Russia, China and Belarus need none for visits of up to 30 days, and of the UAE and Bahrain for up to 90 days within 6 months. It says visa applications are submitted to a Serbian embassy or consulate general abroad or online.

faq.question: Can I enter Serbia from Kosovo?
faq.answer: Only with a Serbian entry stamp. The UK Foreign Office says the authorities in Serbia do not consider the designated crossing points with Kosovo to be official international border crossing points, and that to travel from Kosovo to Serbia you must have a Serbian entry stamp from Belgrade, Niš or Kraljevo airports or from one of Serbia's land border crossings with its other neighbours; without one you are likely to be refused entry.

faq.question: How long can Russian citizens stay in Serbia?
faq.answer: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says Russian holders of ordinary passports need no visa for visits of up to 30 days.

faq.question: Can EU citizens enter Serbia with just an ID card?
faq.answer: Serbia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs pages for Germany, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia and Albania say an ID card can also be used to travel to Serbia, and its page for Montenegro says Montenegrin citizens can travel with an ID card or another identity and citizenship document.

faq.question: Do I have to register with the police in Serbia?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says you must register with the local police where you are staying within 24 hours of arrival, that hotel check-in staff will register you automatically, and that if you do not register you could get a fine and face arrest and a court appearance. Canada says registration will normally be arranged by your hotel or host.

visaPolicy.conditionalWaivers.us-visa.text: On October 30, 2014, the Government of the Republic of Serbia adopted the Decision on visa free entry to the Republic of Serbia for holders of all types of national passports, other than emergency travel documents and travel documents issued in accordance with international conventions, having a valid Schengen, UK and EU Member States' visa, or visa of the United States of America, and for holders of foreign national passports having residence permit in the countries of the Schengen area, EU or the United States of America.

On basis of this decision, the above-mentioned categories of foreign nationals may, without prior visa application, enter, transit and stay in the Republic of Serbia up to 90 days during a six-month period, and within validity of said visas or residence permits.
